newsitem.title: CHINA: China Zhenhai bond offer before end-96.
newsitem.headline: China Zhenhai bond offer before end-96.

text.p: China's Zhenhai Refining and Chemical Co Ltd's plans to issue $200 million of convertible Eurobonds in London before the end of the year, a company official said on Friday.
Zhenhai Refining has said previously that the bonds would be convertible into the company's shares traded in Hong Kong.
ING Barings of the Netherlands and Morgan Stanley would act as lead underwriters for 80 percent of the offer, the official told Reuters by telephone.

The remaining 20 percent of the offering would be taken up by Atlantic Richfield Co of the United States, the official said. ARCO already owned 237.6 million Zhenhai H shares, or 9.9 percent of the company's issued capital.

If the bonds acquired by ARCO and other bondholders were fully converted into H shares, ARCO would own approximately 20 percent of the enlarged share capital of Zhenhai Refining, one of China's largest oil refiners.
The yield and the conversion rate had not been set, the official said, adding that there had been no decision on whether the bonds would have a maturity of five, seven or 10 years.

Net proceeds would be used to finance Zhenhai's expansion programme, which would allow the company to boost its refining capacity to 12 million tonnes a year in 1997 and 16 million tonnes in 2004, Zhenhai has said.
The offer would be subject to approval by shareholders and Chinese and Hong Kong regulatory agencies.
Zhenhai Refining owns and operates a refinery complex in Zhejiang province south of Shanghai.
